lesson.title: Map covered requirements and remaining gaps
lesson.summary: Use standards where supported and explain other compliance solutions.

prerequisites.reason: A standard cannot be mapped to coverage without the applicable requirements.
A gap analysis needs the boundary of the presumption being claimed.

blocks: A **standard coverage matrix** compares each applicable requirement with the parts of a cited standard used and the evidence of actual conformity. Mark uncovered requirements explicitly. A citation alone does not show that your implementation conforms to the cited standard.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 40(1); Annex IV(7)

blocks: **Alternative conformity evidence** can demonstrate an applicable requirement outside a standards presumption. Annex IV(7) asks for applied standards and, where they are not applied, detailed descriptions of the solutions adopted, including other relevant technical specifications. Avoid claiming that voluntary standards are the only possible evidence.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 40(1); Annex IV(7)

blocks: Northbridge uses Standard S for logging but has no cited coverage for oversight. Its alternative record should explain the oversight mechanism, the responsible people, how intervention works, relevant tests and results. This is a practical example of evidence, not an exhaustive statutory test protocol.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 40(1); Annex IV(7)

blocks: Evidence adequacy and assessment-route choice are separate checks. Another procedure may impose standards-dependent route conditions. A documented alternative solution does not automatically preserve an internal-control option for a biometric system or product-law route; check that specific procedure.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 40(1); Annex IV(7)
